# AI Foundation — contracts only

> **Status: `contract-only`.** No LLM inference of any kind. No model gateway client. 9Router is named only as an example of a provider kind. No tool gateway client. Composio is named only as an example of a provider kind. No agent runtime. Hermes, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, OpenClaw, DeepSeek Harness and MiroFish are named only as examples of runtime kinds. No MCP server and no MCP client. No network call, no daemon, no background process and no new dependency.

## The five concepts, kept separate

Conflating any two of these is what makes an integration unreplaceable.

- **capability** — WHAT the system can do. Owned by a LEGO. Stable. Example: `agent.session`.
- **implementation** — HOW a capability is realised. Swappable. Example: a JS implementation or a Rust implementation.
- **provider** — WHERE an implementation is sourced from. Example kinds: model-provider, tool-provider, application-provider.
- **transport** — HOW bytes move. Example: in-process, worker, http, mcp.
- **runtime** — WHERE an agent or system executes. Example kinds: agent-runtime, simulation-runtime.

```
capability -> contract -> operations -> interaction -> implementation -> provider -> transport -> runtime
```

**Anti-pattern:** Declaring `composio.github.repo.read` as a capability. That fuses capability (repo read), provider (Composio) and application (GitHub) into one identifier that cannot be replaced without a rename.

## Provider kinds

| Kind | Contract | What it supplies | Examples |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `model-provider` | `ai.model-gateway` | Supplies inference. Text, embeddings, possibly tool-calling. | a hosted model gateway such as 9Router, a direct vendor API, a local model server |
| `tool-provider` | `ai.tool-gateway` | Supplies callable tools and readable resources to an agent. | a tool/app gateway such as Composio, a local tool pack, an MCP server |
| `application-provider` | `ai.application-provider` | An external application exposed as capabilities. Independent of whichever gateway reaches it. | GitHub, an issue tracker, a chat platform |
| `agent-runtime` | `ai.agent-runtime` | Executes an agent session. Owns the agent loop, not the model. | Hermes, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, OpenClaw, a DeepSeek harness |
| `simulation-runtime` | `ai.agent-runtime` | Executes a scenario or simulation rather than a task-directed agent. | MiroFish |

> A vendor name may appear in this file ONLY inside an `examples` array, and only as an illustration of a provider kind. No vendor may appear in an id, a required field, a code path or a default. If a vendor name is ever needed to make a contract work, the contract is wrong.

## Operations

### `ai.model-gateway`

| Operation | Interaction | Permission | Idempotent |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `models.list` | call | `ai:model:read` | true |
| `model.describe` | call | `ai:model:read` | true |
| `generate` | call | `ai:model:invoke` | false |
| `stream` | stream (block) | `ai:model:invoke` | false |
| `embed` | batch | `ai:model:invoke` | true |
| `countTokens` | call | `ai:model:read` | true |

Cost and latency are OPTIONAL and may be absent or stale. A consumer must treat a missing value as unknown, never as zero. A router that reads absent cost as free will always pick the unpriced model.

### `ai.tool-gateway`

| Operation | Interaction | Permission | Idempotent |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tools.list` | call | `ai:tool:read` | true |
| `tool.describe` | call | `ai:tool:read` | true |
| `tool.call` | call | `ai:tool:invoke` | false |
| `resources.list` | call | `ai:tool:read` | true |
| `resource.read` | call | `ai:tool:read` | true |
| `prompts.list` | call | `ai:tool:read` | true |
| `prompt.get` | call | `ai:tool:read` | true |

`sideEffects` is REQUIRED and one of read-only | writes | destructive | external. It drives the approval contract. A tool that does not declare its side effects must be treated as destructive, because the safe default for an unknown effect is the most restrictive one.

### `ai.agent-runtime`

| Operation | Interaction | Permission | Idempotent |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `create` | call | `ai:agent:create` | false |
| `start` | call | `ai:agent:invoke` | false |
| `send` | call | `ai:agent:invoke` | false |
| `pause` | call | `ai:agent:control` | true |
| `resume` | call | `ai:agent:control` | true |
| `cancel` | call | `ai:agent:control` | true |
| `status` | call | `ai:agent:read` | true |
| `stream` | stream (coalesce) | `ai:agent:read` | false |
| `artifact` | call | `ai:agent:read` | true |
| `close` | call | `ai:agent:control` | true |

`supports.cancellation: false` is a legitimate, declarable answer. A runtime that cannot stop must say so, because the alternative is a cancel that silently does nothing while the caller believes work stopped.

## Application providers

A native integration must never be forced through a gateway. GitHub access via a direct native provider and GitHub access via a tool gateway are two provider bindings of ONE capability set, and the native path must remain available with no gateway configured.

Example decomposition for `github`:

| Capability | Permission | Side effects |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `repo.read` | `app:github:read` | read-only |
| `repo.write` | `app:github:write` | writes |
| `branch.read` | `app:github:read` | read-only |
| `branch.create` | `app:github:write` | writes |
| `commit.create` | `app:github:write` | writes |
| `pr.read` | `app:github:read` | read-only |
| `pr.create` | `app:github:write` | writes |
| `issue.read` | `app:github:read` | read-only |
| `issue.create` | `app:github:write` | writes |
| `actions.read` | `app:github:read` | read-only |
| `webhook.receive` | `app:github:receive` | read-only |

## Session, delegation, events

**Session** `ai.agent-session` — A session record must remain bounded. Storing a transcript inside it would make session size grow without limit and would put model output into the same row as control state — see the artifact contract.

States: `created`, `running`, `waiting`, `paused`, `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`
References: `contextRef`, `artifactRef`, `traceRef`

**Delegation** `ai.agent-delegation` — A child receives only capabilities explicitly listed in `grantedCapabilities`, and that list must be a SUBSET of the parent's. Parent authority never propagates automatically. Automatic propagation means one delegation chain quietly ends in an agent holding every permission in the system.

A budget is required. An unbudgeted delegation can recurse until a resource limit stops it, which on a low-end device means the device stops.

**Events** `ai.agent-events`

No event may carry hidden chain-of-thought, raw prompts, credentials or full model output. An event says what happened and where the detail lives. Reasoning traces are not an audit format and storing them creates a liability with no operational benefit.

`agent.created`, `agent.started`, `agent.waiting`, `agent.paused`, `agent.resumed`, `agent.delegated`, `agent.completed`, `agent.failed`, `agent.cancelled`, `context.loaded`, `context.compacted`, `tool.requested`, `tool.started`, `tool.completed`, `tool.failed`, `decision.created`, `decision.approved`, `decision.rejected`, `approval.requested`, `approval.granted`, `approval.denied`, `artifact.created`, `artifact.updated`, `runtime.connected`, `runtime.disconnected`, `runtime.unavailable`

## Decision and approval

`reasonSummary` is a concise operational justification. Private chain-of-thought must NOT be stored. The auditable question is what was chosen and on what evidence, not what the model internally considered.

**An expired or unanswered approval is a DENY. Defaulting to allow would make the safety layer disappear exactly when the system is under stress or unattended.**

Actions requiring approval: `execute workflow`, `modify credential`, `change system setting`, `delete resource`, `push code`, `merge pull request`, `send external message`

## Artifacts and context

`storageRef` is an opaque reference resolved by the storage domain. The AI contracts must not know whether it is a local file, SQLite row or object store — that is exactly the abstraction the storage domain owns.

Context scopes: `GLOBAL` > `WORKFLOW` > `NODE` > `EXECUTION` > `EVENT` > `AGENT` > `TASK`

There is no mandatory load-everything context. Requiring the whole instance as context makes cost scale with instance size instead of task size, which fails first on exactly the low-end devices this project targets.

## Resources and zero-install

| Profile | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `low-resource` | Runs on a phone, a Termux session or a 1GB VPS. No GPU, no persistent daemon, minimal memory. |
| `standard` | A normal laptop or small server. |
| `high-resource` | Needs substantial CPU or memory; not assumable on a user device. |
| `remote` | Executes elsewhere. Local cost is a network call; availability becomes a real failure mode. |

No external runtime may become a local installation requirement. Every AI provider is optional and remotely satisfiable, because requiring a local agent runtime would exclude the low-end targets the foundation explicitly supports.

### Zero-install is a valid state

```
aiFoundation     ready
modelProvider    not-configured
toolProvider     not-configured
agentRuntime     not-configured
```

Reported as: capability-unavailable with reason 'no inference provider configured'

> The system must never fake inference, never return a canned completion and never pretend a provider exists. It reports that the foundation is ready and no provider is connected. A fake answer is worse than no answer, because the user cannot tell it is fake.

## MCP boundary

```
external world <-> MCP adapter <-> LEGO capability contract <-> implementation
```

- MCP is an interoperability ADAPTER at the edge. It must never become the internal application architecture.
- No internal LEGO may call another LEGO over MCP. Internal communication stays CALL/EVENT/STREAM/BATCH over the local dispatcher, as ADR-0004 requires.
- MCP concepts map ONTO the tool gateway contract; the tool gateway is not defined in MCP terms. If MCP changes, one adapter changes.
- Capabilities are exported explicitly and individually. There is no export-everything switch, because the set of capabilities safe to hand to an external client is never the full set.

**No MCP server, client, adapter or dependency exists in this repository.**

## Transport routing

| When | Transport | Mechanism |
| --- | --- | --- |
| same process | `in-process` | direct dispatcher |
| local event | `in-process` | event dispatcher |
| process boundary | `worker` | IPC / worker adapter |
| remote service | `remote` | HTTP or a provider-defined protocol |
| external interoperability | `mcp` | MCP adapter |

Never force every call through HTTP. An HTTP hop between two objects in one process is the most expensive available way to call a function.

A transport advertises which interaction classes it can carry. The OPERATION owns its interaction class; a transport that cannot carry it is simply not eligible. A transport must never silently downgrade a STREAM to a CALL — the caller asked for incremental output and would instead wait for a single late response.

## Rust

Rust remains an implementation choice beneath these contracts, exactly as ADR-0005 states. No Rust is written in this phase. Rust is never chosen merely to demonstrate that Rust exists, and must never require a compiler on an end-user device.
